plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated hill session for strength and trail adaptation.
Features longer, more varied runs (13km and 174min) that build aerobic base and durability.
Provides a more balanced approach to training, combining easy runs with targeted efforts.
plan_b_advantages: Emphasizes consistent easy running, which can be beneficial for recovery and maintaining overall fitness.
Incorporates a tempo run, which can improve lactate threshold – a key factor in running faster.
reasoning: Plan A is better suited for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates more targeted hill work and a longer, more structured hill session (55 minutes) alongside longer, easier runs. This directly addresses the demands of trail running – navigating varied terrain and building strength – which Plan B largely neglects. While Plan B focuses heavily on consistent easy running, it lacks the specific stimulus needed to improve speed and power, crucial for a faster runner. Plan A’s inclusion of a controlled hill session is a key differentiator.
